text:
maya: Heads-up — APAC pool 'apac-3' saw a burst of ECC correctable errors starting ~01:10 UTC. Rate jumped from ~0.02% to ~0.8% over 10m. Roughly 4 cards across 3 nodes showing activity. Low-priority Dedicated customers reporting token latency jitter. Do we want immediate surgical evict of the affected cards or a watch-and-wait + routing fallback?

samir: Pulling telemetry now. Quick snapshot:
- nodes: nodeA (card1), nodeB (card0,card2), nodeC (card0 low).
- ecc_count last 10m: nodeA/card1=320, nodeB/card0=280, nodeB/card2=95, nodeC/card0=12.
- driver: 530.xx, GPUs A100-80GB. No recent reboots, no PCIe x16 errors. Two cards look flappy (120/5m, 95/5m). Correlates with long-seq inference jobs.

jess: If it's two flapping cards then targeted surgical eviction makes sense instead of pool wide. Options: 1) immediate surgical drain those cards (migrate on-node pods off the cards, keep node up), 2) trigger routing fallback (route ~5% traffic to eu-west) and open HW ticket for replacement. Which minimizes customer impact?

leo: Quick cost/impact note: surgical drain -> ~2h capacity hit per node while pods resettle and warm KV caches. Cross-region fallback -> higher egress/cost but less local capacity loss and preserves SLAs for high-priority traffic. My vote: surgical now to stop jitter for Dedicated customers, and use fallback only if we see >3 nodes affected. Also we should tighten auto-drain thresholds: require 3 consecutive 5m buckets > 50 correctables before auto-drain flips.

adele: @infra-bot please paste the full alert timeline + node ids and patch-levels. Also can we mark affected traffic as low-priority T1 so it gets shed during maintenance?

infra-bot: Alert summary: ECC burst detected 2026-03-15T01:10Z; affected nodes [nodeA,nodeB,nodeC]; spike persisted ~12m; anomaly score 7.2; link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/2364800000 (automated).

opsbot: Proposed command to start surgical drain for specific cards (dry-run validated in staging):
```
fleetctl drain --node nodeB --cards 0,2 --mode surgical --grace 20m --route-fallback eu-west=5%
```
This will cordon card slices, evacuate pods, and apply fallback routing override.

samir: Did a dry-run on staging for that exact command, pods migrated cleanly and the KV cache warmed in ~8m for the biggest workloads. Suggest also applying `no-schedule:hardware-swap` label to nodes we touch to prevent new allocations: `kubectl label node nodeB no-schedule=hardware-swap`.

jess: Decision: execute surgical drains on nodeA/card1 and nodeB/cards0,2 now. I'll kick the commands and watch the migrations. Hardware-ops: please create replacement ticket and reserve spares for the pool (serials attached in ticket). We'll hold fallback routing in reserve at 5% if migrations fail to restore SLOs.

hardware-ops: @jess acknowledged. Creating ticket SWP-APAC-482, scheduling swap. If parts not on-rack ETA~48h, will escalate to spare pool.

maya: Thanks everyone. Action items: 1) run `fleetctl drain` surgical on nodeA/card1 + nodeB/cards0,2, 2) patch runbook: auto-drain requires 3x consecutive 5m buckets > 50 correctables before auto-trigger, keep routing fallback at 5% reserve, 3) open HW ticket and tag nodes for replacement. I'll update the incident channel when drains complete. :thumbsup:
